newsitem.title: UK: Simon sees flat profit, to sell Access unit.
newsitem.headline: Simon sees flat profit, to sell Access unit.

text.p: British engineering group Simon Engineering Plc warned that its full year profits were unlikely to be different from last year and said it planned to sell its Access division in order to cut debt.

"It is anticipated that Simon's results for the full year will not be substantially different from those achieved in 1995," as a result of high borrowing and trading losses from Access UK, chairman Michael Davies said in a statement.
Simon shares were down 9-1/2 pence to 39-1/2 pence by 0835 GMT after touching a low of 39 pence on the news.
Simon said net debt had increased to 82.7 million stg from 75.1 million stg at December 31, 1995.
It said the decision to sell its Access unit came after failing to secure necessary new loan facilities.
Gleacher NatWest Inc of New York has been put in charge of the sale and a further announcement is expected by the end of the year.
"The board is confident that with the debt position resolved the overall prospects for the group will be enhanced," the company said in a statement.
It said, in the absence of unforeseen circumstances, it intended to pay out a dividend for 1996.
Simon reported pretax profits for the six months to June 30 up 55 percent to 3.7 million stg but passed on its interim dividend, as it did last year.

It said after the sale of Access, lower gearing and interest charges, and the lack of losses from Access UK "will enable Simon to exploit fully the undoubted opportunities for growth that exist in the storage and process engineering divisions."
